tool_analysis:
1) Step Analysis:
The recorded steps walk through the complete Magento 1.9 admin flow to create a new Simple Product with the Default attribute set. The flow:
- Navigates to the admin catalog product URL (which redirects to login when not authenticated).
- Logs in via the login form using the provided admin username and password.
- Lands on the Manage Products grid.
- Initiates the Add Product flow via the Add Product button.
- On the Create Product Settings page, selects an Attribute Set (Default) and Product Type (Simple Product), then clicks Continue.
- On the New Product (Default) form, fills required General tab fields (Name, Description, Short Description, SKU, Weight, Status, Visibility).
- Switches to Prices tab, sets Price and Tax Class.
- Switches to Inventory tab, sets Qty and Stock Availability.
- Clicks Save, then is redirected back to the Manage Products grid where the success message and new product row are visible.

2) Task Definition:
Define a reusable, deterministic tool that, given product attributes and configuration (attribute set, product type, name, descriptions, SKU, weight, price, tax class, quantity, status, visibility, stock availability), will:
- Navigate to the Magento admin catalog product URL
- Log in using known credentials
- Start the add-product flow (type + attribute set)
- Fill the required fields across General, Prices, and Inventory tabs
- Save the product
The previous failure was due to brittle login selectors. This tool must specifically avoid the failing selector `input[name="login[username]"][type="text"]` and instead rely on stable identifiers (here: elementHash plus generic click/input actions) or an agentic step if necessary.

3) Action Plan (high level steps):
1. Navigation to admin catalog product list URL.
2. Login sequence on "Log in to Admin Panel" page:
   - Input username into the username field (element_hash 3597a5c5e6).
   - Input password into the password field (element_hash 1c47a5217e).
   - Click the Login button (element_hash 6831836d17).
3. On Manage Products grid:
   - Click Add Product button (element_hash e779c2f1fc) to go to Create Product Settings.
4. On Create Product Settings page:
   - Select the Attribute Set dropdown (element_hash d2ae05bcc3) option matching provided attribute set name.
   - Select the Product Type dropdown (element_hash 9f39b707f1) option matching provided product type name.
   - Click Continue button (element_hash bd059f9b39) to go to New Product form.
5. On New Product (Default) form – General tab:
   - Input Name in Name text field (element_hash df3020a86b).
   - Input Description in Description textarea (element_hash 6aec08c625).
   - Input Short Description in Short Description textarea (element_hash 4b38ca02b1).
   - Input SKU in SKU field (element_hash 1349f1ca81).
   - Input Weight in Weight field (element_hash d929abfc8b).
   - Select Status dropdown (element_hash d7baed0536) option matching provided status text.
   - Select Visibility dropdown (element_hash 2d6f7788e8) option matching provided visibility text.
6. Switch to Prices tab:
   - Click the Prices tab link (element_hash 86ed7ee82d).
   - Input Price in Price field (element_hash e457e89369).
   - Select Tax Class dropdown (element_hash 1d20c0f068) option matching provided tax class text.
7. Switch to Inventory tab:
   - Click the Inventory tab link (element_hash 71d44f34a7).
   - Input Qty in Qty field (element_hash 15f8e67c9f).
   - Select Stock Availability dropdown (element_hash 09a76db7af) option matching provided stock availability text.
8. Save product:
   - Click the Save button (element_hash 8677f5f4ee).

4) Variable Identification (tool inputs):
Based on the steps and required Magento fields, extract these parameters:
- login_username (string, required) – although currently fixed as "admin", keeping it parameterized is safer.
- login_password (string, required) – currently "password123".
- attribute_set (string, required) – visible text of attribute set dropdown, e.g. "Default", "Books & Music".
- product_type (string, required) – visible text of product type, e.g. "Simple Product".
- name (string, required) – product Name.
- description (string, required) – Description.
- short_description (string, required) – Short Description.
- sku (string, required) – SKU.
- weight (string, required) – weight text; simple string to avoid locale complexity.
- status (string, required, enum) – e.g. "Enabled" or "Disabled".
- visibility (string, required, enum) – e.g. "Not Visible Individually", "Catalog", "Search", "Catalog, Search".
- price (string, required) – numeric string for Price (e.g. "39.99").
- tax_class (string, required, enum) – e.g. "None", "Taxable Goods", "Shipping", "Tax Exempt".
- qty (string, required) – quantity text (e.g. "25").
- stock_availability (string, required, enum) – e.g. "In Stock", "Out of Stock".

All these fields are required by Magento for a minimal valid simple product based on the extraction results (General: Name, Description, Short Description, SKU, Weight, Status, Visibility; Prices: Price, Tax Class; Inventory: Qty). Login credentials are required for access.

5) Step Optimization & Determinism:
- Navigation: Always start via a navigation step to `http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_product/` as demonstrated.
- Login: Prior attempts failed using a brittle CSS selector. Here we will not attempt to define CSS; instead, we will use the recorded element_hash values with the generic `input` and `click` actions. These have been demonstrated to work and avoid reliance on CSS name attributes that may vary. If timing becomes an issue, a single wait step can be added after navigation.
- Create Product Settings / New Product forms: Rely on element_hash for selects, inputs, and buttons, as these correspond to unique and stable DOM elements on Magento.
- Tab navigation: Prices and Inventory tab anchors have stable element_hash values and are clicked deterministically.
- No exploratory actions: We omit grid filters, sorting, and optional metadata because they are not part of the core task (creating a product). We also skip extraction steps used only for analysis.
- URL optimizations: While the product creation form URL encodes attribute set and product type (`/new/set/4/type/simple/`), using direct URL manipulation would bypass the Create Product Settings interaction, which is explicitly part of the required demo. Therefore we keep the UI interaction path rather than replacing it with URL manipulation.

The resulting tool focuses solely on the end-to-end creation of a simple product with configurable fields and robust, elementHash-based interactions, explicitly fixing the previous login selector failure.
name: tool_create_product_v5
description: Create a new simple product in Magento Admin starting from the catalog product URL, including login, product type & attribute set selection, filling required fields, and saving the product.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Admin catalog product URL, which will redirect to login if not authenticated.
Enter the admin username into the login username field on the Magento Admin login page using a robust element hash instead of brittle CSS selectors.
Enter the admin password into the login password field on the Magento Admin login page using a robust element hash.
Click the Login button to submit the admin login form and access the Manage Products grid.
Click the Add Product button on the Manage Products grid to initiate the add-product flow and open Create Product Settings.
Select the desired Attribute Set on the Create Product Settings page using its visible text.
Select the desired Product Type on the Create Product Settings page using its visible text.
Click the Continue button on the Create Product Settings page to load the full New Product form.
Fill the General tab Name field with the provided product name.
Fill the General tab Description textarea with the provided description.
Fill the General tab Short Description textarea with the provided short description.
Fill the General tab SKU field with the provided SKU.
Fill the General tab Weight field with the provided weight value.
Set the General tab Status field using the provided status value.
Set the General tab Visibility field using the provided visibility value.
Switch to the Prices tab of the New Product form by clicking the Prices tab link.
Fill the Prices tab Price field with the provided price value.
Set the Prices tab Tax Class field using the provided tax class value.
Switch to the Inventory tab of the New Product form by clicking the Inventory tab link.
Fill the Inventory tab Qty field with the provided quantity value.
Set the Inventory tab Stock Availability field using the provided stock availability value.
Click the Save button at the top of the New Product form to save the product and return to the Manage Products grid.
